questions.subject: ANTHROPOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: examine kinship using anthropological evidence

stimulus.body: A researcher maps the terms people use for relatives and finds that the category cousin is divided into several distinct named relations.

questions.stem: Which statement about kinship is best supported by the account?

options.text: Kinship is the system of relationships and categories by which people define and organize family ties.
Kinship is the study of the physical process of human reproduction.
options.misconception: The multiple terms for cousins show that the culture classifies relatives more finely than a single label.

options.text: Kinship is a set of laws governing the ownership of land in a modern state.
options.misconception: It reduces kinship to biology, ignoring the cultural classification of relations.

options.text: Kinship refers only to relationships created by marriage and excludes blood relatives.

questions.explanation: It wrongly limits kinship to in-laws, excluding consanguineal ties.
questions.hint: Kinship systems vary widely in which relatives are grouped together and how they are named.

options.misconception: It assigns the term to family law, a different institution.

questions.subject: ANTHROPOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: examine unilineal descent using anthropological evidence
